sections.title: Right now
lines: Pre-race growth. Green flag Sat 10/17 6:30 PM CT (in 2d 8h).
Sold 8,800 contracts so far; 29,652 more resting on the book. Premium collected $811.
Worst line is -$889. The glide target right now is -$400, so it is $489 short; the final target is -$100 by T-60.
Backstop is ON for Jesse Love, Justin Allgaier: their lines are under -$400, so they stop adding until the others catch up.
Prices follow Bovada, refreshed every 5m (last 3m ago). Covers 37 of 39 drivers.
Bot is healthy: heartbeat 5s old, no errors.

sections.title: Lagging sides
lines: Sheldon Creed: sold 0, 1,700 behind the leader. Cheapest row 8c; the crowd has been buying at 8c; fair 7.1c. Already at its floor (about 8c); it will not go lower unless the crowd price or fair drops.

Brent Crews: sold 70, 1,630 behind the leader. Cheapest row 10c; the crowd has been buying at 10c; fair 5.2c. Already at its floor (about 10c); it will not go lower unless the crowd price or fair drops.

Corey Day: sold 198, 1,502 behind the leader. Cheapest row 9c; the crowd has been buying at 9c; fair 7.1c. Already at its floor (about 9c); it will not go lower unless the crowd price or fair drops. Last hold reason (13m ago): the next cent down (9c to 8c) would go below the bot's price floor (the highest of the crowd's clearing price 7.2c, the crowd's best ask, and fair minus a small allowance), so it holds at 9c.

Carson Kvapil: sold 656, 1,044 behind the leader. Cheapest row 14c; the crowd has been buying at 13c; fair 11.7c. It can step down 1c at a time, to no lower than about 13c, after 20 min with no fill, at most one step per 15 min. Last step: none seen.
Justin Allgaier: sold 1,248, 452 behind the leader. Nothing is resting on it: the backstop has stopped it adding.

The bot checks every 30s; it logs a market snapshot every 10 min. Rows already resting are not repriced when the sportsbook moves; only new rows use the fresh price. A step is skipped if filling the new row in full would push a line under the backstop or the glide target.
From T-360 (glide start) the price-step rule is on for lagging drivers so they can sell into the late rush of crowd orders.

sections.title: Next wave of contracts
lines: Trigger: when a driver's current wave is 90% filled and a full fill would keep his line above the gate, the bot posts the next wave (sizes 1,000/750/750 for contenders/midfield/long shots per wave), priced one cent above the last fill. The book's worst line must also be above the backstop, and free cash above the $1,300 floor.
Right now it is the growth phase (before T-360): the gate is loose (-$1,000) and the number of contracts is limited by what the crowd is likely to buy and by free cash.
Brandon Jones: 3 waves so far, 1,230 contracts offered in all; the latest (390 at 5c) is 23% filled.
Sammy Smith: 2 waves so far, 1,528 contracts offered in all; the latest (778 at 7c) is 0% filled.
Waves stop at T-60.

sections.title: Tightening
lines: The risk glide starts at T-360 (Sat 10/17 12:30 PM CT, in 2d 2h). Until then the limit on the worst line is the backstop (-$400). From then the limit slides in a straight line to -$100 at T-60 (Sat 10/17 5:30 PM CT).

When the worst line is under the target the bot: blocks any post whose full fill would break the target, shrinks resting size over the room in place, buys back the worst line cheaply (only when each dollar spent lifts the line 2.0x or more, up to 3 per loop, budget 50% of banked premium), and starts selling to close gaps from T-90.
Preview: if the worst line is still -$889 at T-360, the glide would have to bring it up by about $489 to reach the first target.
Even-up (lagging drivers re-priced to fair) from T-60; the take window (sell to close gaps) from T-20 to the green flag.
Checkpoints: T-2880, T-1440, T-360, T-180, T-120, T-60, T-20 before the green flag.
At the green flag the bot keeps the resting orders and hands over to the in-race engine.

sections.title: Will it adapt on its own?
lines: Yes, on its own: new waves for popular drivers, price steps on lagging contenders, the backstop that stops a heavy driver, and the glide that tightens the worst line toward -$100.

No, it will not: reprice a resting row when Bovada moves, or buy back a driver for any reason except the glide's cheap-lift rule. If Bovada's field drops below 80% coverage the bot just holds what it has.

The one thing that depends on the market: the worst line is -$889 against a -$100 final target. Premium from the rest of the field and fills on lagging drivers lift it; the glide's buybacks cover what is left, within their budget. It might not fully close.
I only read the bot's settings, state and log. I cannot see its next decision, only the rules it follows.
